title: Chickadee — reads pages aloud, on your machine
excerpt: The speech model runs in your browser. Nothing you read is ever uploaded.
content_html:
Chickadeeruns entirely on your machineLocal · Open source · Free forever

Any page,
read aloud,
locally.

A browser extension that reads web pages in a natural voice. The speech model runs on your own computer, not a server. It works offline and is free. Nothing it reads is ever uploaded, and there is no account, no API key, and nothing to pay for.

Every other text-to-speech extension sends the page you're reading to a server. Chickadee doesn't. It runs Kokoro, an eighty-two million parameter speech model, right here in the browser. The words you are hearing right now were made by that model, on this machine. It is open source, and it is free forever. The voice downloads once, about three hundred and ten megabytes, and then it works offline. Install it, open any article, and press Alt plus R.

fig. 2 — seeing it work

It highlights the page you’re already on.

The article itself, with the spoken sentence lit as it goes.

Local and private

The model executes in your browser via WebGPU. There is no server to send anything to, so there is nothing to leak.

Reads the real page

Sentences are highlighted on the page itself, right where you are reading. Right-click any word to start from there.

Works offline

One ~310 MB voice download on first use. After that, it never touches the network again. You can use it on a plane, in a tunnel, or in the wilderness.

Free forever

Open source, with nothing to pay for — no subscription, no upsell. The voice is a small open model that lives in your browser, and always will.

Install it and press ⌥ R

Chrome-based browsers · requires WebGPU

Add to Chrome

Needs a WebGPU-capable browser and machine. Chickadee checks on first run and tells you plainly if yours can’t run it.
